title: bank israel cuts rates third straight meeting inflation stays low 2026 09 01
text:
JERUSALEM, Sept 1 (Reuters) - The Bank of Israel cut ​interest rates for a third straight meeting on Tuesday, taking borrowing costs to their lowest level in nearly ‌four years, and signalled more easing could follow if inflation remains subdued.
Diverging from the broader global trend of tighter monetary policy, the central bank cut its benchmark rate (ILINR=ECI)
, opens new tab
 by 25 basis points to 3.25%, the lowest level since late 2022.
It cut rates in November and January, paused amid the conflict with ​Iran and concerns over supply-driven inflation, and resumed easing in May and July.
"We've seen the last few months inflation has ​been coming down," Deputy Governor Andrew Abir told Reuters after the decision. "We didn't really see a compelling reason ⁠not to continue with the process of reducing interest rates."
Tuesday's move went against the majority view in a Reuters poll. Eight of ​14 economists expected rates to remain unchanged, while six forecast a 25-basis-point cut.
Annual inflation stood at 1.5% in July, well within the bank's ​1% to 3% target range and below its preferred 2% level.
"Do we need to run interest rates that are 3 1/2% to keep inflation at the middle of our range? No," Abir said.
The rate cut was welcomed by manufacturers, while Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said borrowing costs should fall further.
Markets widely ​expect at least one more rate cut, and Bank of Israel economists project rates at 3% by mid-2027. Abir said the outlook ​depends on inflation, geopolitical developments and how financial markets and the economy respond to the latest move.
"If inflation sort of stabilises and goes back up ‌a ⁠bit, we could pause around these levels, or if it continues going down, or if there's a continued appreciation of the (shekel) currency, we could continue reducing rates," Abir said.
"It very much depends on the data that we see going forward."
The central bank noted that although Israel's economy rebounded in the second quarter, growing an annualised 15.4%, "net of production abroad by Israeli companies, GDP in the second quarter was (just) ​3.8 percent higher than in ​the fourth quarter of 2025 ⁠in annual terms."
Leader Capital Markets Chief Economist Jonathan Katz said he thought the cut was a close call for policymakers and the next reduction would likely be in November rather than at the October ​21 meeting, less than a week before Israeli elections.
"A positive election outcome is likely to support ​shekel appreciation and ⁠therefore a possible additional rate cut by end-year — assuming no ugly inflation prints," Katz said. "But we are approaching the terminal rate of 3.0%."
The shekel weakened 1.1% against the dollar to 3.022 after the decision. It remains about 5% stronger so far in 2026. Tel Aviv shares gained ⁠as much ​as 0.7%.
Morgan Stanley's Georgi Deyanov said he expects one final rate cut in ​November, with rates holding at 3% through 2027. Higher than expected fiscal spending could delay or prevent further easing, although "a sustainable de-escalation in geopolitical tensions opening room for ​additional and more front-loaded rate cuts than in our base case," he added.
